subject: Clarify billing boundaries for long-context streams + sample worksheet
messages:
From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@acmevision.com>

Cc: marco.ruiz@acmevision.com

Subject: Billing for very long streams / sample invoice request

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the latency and quality look promising. We have two billing / packaging questions the procurement team needs answered before we can move to the legal + signature stage:

1) We send long OCR/ingest sessions that average ~90k tokens per job and occasionally spike to 150k. How will those be billed under the token-windowing rules? Is there an explicit per-request cap or do you simply round up to the nearest billing quantum?

2) We rely heavily on streaming where partial responses are continuously emitted and the client keeps a rolling context. Does Redwood bill streaming as per final token count, or on per-chunk transmission? How do KV cache hits (prefix reuse) affect the unit calculation?

3) We need an example invoice with our usage profile (attached) and a sample monthly cost at current list pricing and two discounted scenarios (10% and 20% for a committed pilot). Can you return a worksheet that shows how rounding/minimums apply to our spikes?

Attached: acme_request_packet.pdf (usage samples + PO draft)

Can you loop in billing/finance so we have something to give Legal today? We are targeting a signed pilot by next week.

Thanks,
Alyssa
Procurement Lead, AcmeVision

Subject: Re: Billing for very long streams / sample invoice request

Alyssa — thanks for the packet and the clear asks. Looping Vanessa (AM) and Ben (billing lead) for detail; quick summary from my side below and we'll attach a worked worksheet by EOD.

High-level answers (short):
- Long requests: we meter at per-token granularity but apply a billing quantum of 256 tokens for per-call accounting (requests are rounded up to the nearest 256 token unit). That means a 90k token request is billed as ceiling(90000/256)*256 tokens.
- Streaming / partials: we bill tokens actually generated & received by the customer. If a stream is aborted mid-response, only the tokens emitted before the abort count.
- KV/prefix cache: when a request reuses a cached prefix on the server side, we only bill for the incremental tokens generated (we do not double-charge the cached tokens). However, there is a 1-call minimum quantum that still applies to avoid pathological sub-token billing.

Pending items:
- Ben will provide a worksheet that models your weekly spike pattern and shows invoice examples under list pricing vs 10% and 20% pilot concession.
- Vanessa will confirm whether the 3-month pilot concession can be captured as an amendment to the quote (yes) and whether we can add a one-time invoice credit if spikes exceed projections.

I attached a short explainer and will follow up with the calc sheet.

Best,
Soojin

Alyssa — I built the worksheet (attached: billing_sample_calcs.xlsx) and included three worked examples. Key points and explicit numeric examples follow so you can validate the math quickly.

Important: Redwood uses a per-token metering base but reports and invoices are computed after rounding to a billing quantum (Q) = 256 tokens per-call. We also have a per-request floor of 512 tokens when requests are <512 tokens (so short calls are not billed at a micro level). For long calls the floor is irrelevant because the rounding dominates.

Worked example 1 — steady: 90,000 tokens in a single request- Q = 256- billed_units = ceiling(90000 / 256) = ceiling(351.5625) = 352 units- billed_tokens = 352 * 256 = 90,112 tokens billed- delta due to rounding = 112 tokens (~0.12% overhead)

Worked example 2 — spike: 150,200 tokens in a single request- billed_units = ceiling(150200/256) = ceiling(586.71875) = 587 units- billed_tokens = 587 * 256 = 150,272 tokens billed- delta = 72 tokens (~0.048% overhead)

Worked example 3 — streaming aborted after 23,400 tokens emitted from a 60k generation attempt- billed_units = ceiling(23400/256) = 92 units- billed_tokens = 92 * 256 = 23,552 tokens billed- Note: we bill for emitted tokens only; aborted generations do not incur billing for un-emitted tokens.

KV cache example:
- If you send a 4k prefix that is cacheable and then send a 3k incremental with reuse, the cache saves the 4k (no re-billing for that prefix) and you are billed only for the 3k plus rounding: ceiling(3000/256) * 256 = 12 units * 256 = 3072 tokens billed.

Pilot concession and invoice handling (summary):
- For the 3-month pilot we can apply a volume discount entered on the Quote. With your expected monthly committed baseline (see sheet) we can do 20% off list for the first 90 days. After that we revert to list unless a multiyear commit is signed.
- We can also include an overage protection clause: if a single month exceeds 150% of forecasted usage we apply a one-time invoice credit equal to the overage above 150% (to a capped amount).

I attached both the calc sheet and a redlined quote (redwood_quote_ACMV-2025-03.pdf). Let me know if you want the numbers at 10% vs 20% in separate columns — I included both in the sheet.

Ben
Head of Billing | Redwood Inference
